title: Settings
subtitle: Profiles, indexers, download clients, identification sources, and notifications.

home.welcomeBody: Pick a section from the side nav. Each sub-page configures one slice of the acquisition pipeline.

placeholder.knownBody: This Settings sub-page is documented in the spec but hasn't shipped yet. The slice that wires it up against its REST surface is coming.
placeholder.unknownBody: No Settings section is registered at this path. Pick another from the side nav.

connect.title: Notifications
connect.subtitle: Outbound notification targets routed through Apprise. Each row carries event subscriptions and a redacted URL — the raw URL is encrypted at rest.

webhookDoc.body: Building a Notifiarr / Recyclarr / Homepage integration? Romarr ships a per-event JSON payload reference.

search.label: Search notifications
search.noMatches: No notifications match the active search.

empty.title: No notifications configured
empty.body: Add an Apprise URL to start routing OnGrab / OnImport / OnFail / health events outbound.

create.subhead: One row per Apprise endpoint. The URL is encrypted at rest; you'll only see the redacted form afterwards.
create.urlHint: Apprise schemas: discord://, slack://, mailto://, gotify://, ntfy://, … See the Apprise wiki for the full list.

toggles.onGrab: On Grab — release queued for download
toggles.onImport: On Import — release added to library
toggles.onUpgrade: On Upgrade — better release replaced an older one
toggles.onFail: On Fail — download or import failed
toggles.onHealthIssue: On Health Issue — system health event
toggles.onDatUpdate: On DAT Update — DAT cache refreshed
toggles.onGameAdded: On Game Added — new Game row created

delete.confirmBody: Future events won't be routed to {{name}}.

downloadClients.title: Download Clients
downloadClients.subtitle: Torrent + Usenet clients Romarr hands grabs to. Each client carries its own protocol enables and lifecycle policy.

search.label: Search download clients
search.noMatches: No download clients match the active search.

empty.title: No download clients configured
empty.body: Add a qBittorrent or SABnzbd client to start grabbing. Other clients (Transmission, Deluge, NZBGet) land in v1+.

create.subhead: qBittorrent + SABnzbd are the MVP-supported clients; Transmission / Deluge / NZBGet are scaffolded for v1+.

delete.confirmBody: Romarr won't hand grabs to {{name}} anymore. In-progress downloads stay where they are.

datSources.title: DAT Sources
datSources.subtitle: Authoritative DAT databases loaded into Romarr's hash cache. Hash matches against these entries are the highest-authority identification signal.

empty.title: No DAT sources loaded yet
empty.body: Trigger the dat-update task under System > Tasks to ingest the first DAT bundle.

datSources.refreshHint: Re-run the dat-update task under System > Tasks to refresh.

qualityDefinitions.title: Quality Definitions
qualityDefinitions.subtitle: Per-platform file size bounds. Min/max bytes drive the search-engine quality gate and the importer's reject-too-small floor — re-encodes outside this range are dropped.

empty.title: No platforms configured
empty.body: Apply a Platform Pack first under Settings > Platforms.

qualityDefinitions.platformNoFormats: No formats defined for this platform yet — apply a Platform Pack to populate them.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.subtitle: Six profile types drive every grab / upgrade / import decision. Each library carries one profile of each type; profiles are reusable across libraries.
profiles.comingSoonBody: {{tab}} profile management lands in a follow-up slice. The backend endpoint isn't shipped yet — check back once the relevant spec lands.

dump.subtitle: Filter releases by dump quality. The allowed list pins which dump statuses qualify; the four toggles open the door to specific risky variants.

empty.title: No dump profiles
empty.body: Romarr ships a factory-default catalogue. If this list is empty, run the seed migration.

delete.confirmBody: Libraries bound to {{name}} will need a replacement profile before their next decision runs.
delete.factoryBlocked: Factory-default profiles can't be deleted; reset them with the seed migration if needed.

dump.editorHint: Allowed-list multi-select + four flag toggles + revision picker land in a follow-up slice.

create.subhead: List the dump statuses this profile accepts. The four toggles open specific risky variants.

errors.name: Pick a profile name first.
errors.allowedEmpty: Allowed dump statuses can't be empty.

naming.subtitle: Filename + folder layout templates. Each library binds to one Naming profile; the convention determines the token vocabulary the template can reference.

empty.title: No naming profiles
empty.body: Romarr ships a factory-default catalogue. If this list is empty, run the seed migration.

delete.confirmBody: Libraries bound to {{name}} will need a replacement profile before their next decision runs.
delete.factoryBlocked: Factory-default profiles can't be deleted; reset them with the seed migration if needed.

naming.editorHint: Click Preview on any profile to render its template against the synthetic sample release (Sonic the Hedgehog (USA).md). The full template editor lands in a follow-up slice.

create.subhead: Pick a convention + edit the Jinja template that builds the rendered filename. Tokens like {{ Game.Title }} and {{ Release.Region }} resolve at import time.
create.templateHint: Jinja template using whitelisted tokens (Game.Title / Release.Region / Release.Languages / Dump.Extension / …). Use the Preview button after saving to see the rendered output.

flags.platformSubfolder: Wrap each platform in its own sub-folder
flags.multiDiscSubfolder: Group multi-disc sets in a sub-folder

region.subtitle: Region preferences for selecting between releases of the same game. Priorities resolve ties (USA-first, EUR-first, etc.); excluded regions are dropped outright.

empty.title: No region profiles
empty.body: Romarr ships a factory-default catalogue. If this list is empty, run the seed migration.

delete.confirmBody: Libraries bound to {{name}} will need a replacement profile before their next decision runs.
delete.factoryBlocked: Factory-default profiles can't be deleted; reset them with the seed migration if needed.

region.editorHint: Drag-list editor for priorities + multi-select for excluded regions lands in a follow-up slice.

create.subhead: Priorities are most-preferred first. Excluded regions are dropped outright. Comma-separated, ISO 3-letter codes (USA, EUR, JPN, …).

errors.name: Pick a profile name first.
errors.emptyNoFallback: Priorities can't be empty when fallback is disabled — the profile would reject every release.
errors.overlap: Region(s) appear in both priorities and exclude: {{regions}}.

language.subtitle: Language preferences. Required languages must all be present on a release for it to qualify; preferred languages tie-break between qualifying releases.

empty.title: No language profiles
empty.body: Romarr ships a factory-default catalogue. If this list is empty, run the seed migration.

delete.confirmBody: Libraries bound to {{name}} will need a replacement profile before their next decision runs.
delete.factoryBlocked: Factory-default profiles can't be deleted; reset them with the seed migration if needed.

language.editorHint: Required + preferred drag-list editors land in a follow-up slice.

create.subhead: Required languages must all be present on a release. Preferred languages tie-break between qualifying releases. Use ISO 639-1 codes (en, fr, ja, …).
create.languageHint: Comma-separated, ISO 639-1 codes. Leave blank for no requirement.

quality.subtitle: Each library binds to one Quality profile. The profile lists the formats Romarr will accept (allowed), the one it prefers as the upgrade target (preferred), and the ceiling beyond which it won't keep upgrading (upgrade-until).

empty.title: No quality profiles
empty.body: Romarr ships a factory-default catalogue. If this list is empty, run the seed migration.

delete.confirmBody: Libraries bound to {{name}} will need a replacement profile before their next decision runs.
delete.factoryBlocked: Factory-default profiles can't be deleted; reset them with the seed migration if needed.

quality.editorHint: The full Quality profile editor (drag-drop allowed-formats list, preferred / upgrade-until pickers, DAT + archive toggles) lands in a follow-up slice.

create.subhead: List the formats this profile accepts, then pick one as preferred + one as the upgrade ceiling. Both must be in the allowed list.
create.allowedFormatsHint: Comma-separated list of format strings from your platform packs. e.g. ``cartridge, cd_chd, cd_iso``.

errors.name: Pick a profile name first.
errors.preferredNotAllowed: Preferred format must be in the allowed list.
errors.upgradeNotAllowed: Upgrade-until format must be in the allowed list.

create.successBody: {{name}} is now available to bind to a library.

customFormats.title: Custom Formats
customFormats.subtitle: Score modifiers Romarr applies to release candidates. Each format owns a score and a list of conditions evaluated against the parsed release.

empty.title: No custom formats
empty.body: Romarr ships a factory-default catalogue. If this list is empty, run the seed migration.

delete.confirmBody: Releases won't pick up the score modifier from {{name}} anymore.
delete.factoryBlocked: Factory-default formats can't be deleted; reset them with the seed migration if needed.

customFormats.builderHint: The visual condition builder (add / remove conditions, OR-grouping) lands in a follow-up slice. For now POST /api/v3/customformat to create new formats.

mediaManagement.title: Media Management
mediaManagement.subtitle: Library destinations on disk plus their lifecycle policy and per-library exporter switches. Each library binds to one of every profile type (Quality / Region / Dump / Language / Naming).

empty.title: No libraries configured
empty.body: Add a library to point Romarr at a destination directory. The first library is the operator's primary acquisition target.

create.subhead: One row per destination directory. Profile picks bind the library to its decision matrix; lifecycle policy controls what happens to the source after import.
create.pathHint: Absolute path on the Romarr host. Make sure Romarr's user has read/write + execute on the directory.

flags.useHardlinks: Use hardlinks where possible (cross-FS falls back to copy)

delete.confirmBody: Releases bound to {{name}} will need a replacement library. The directory on disk is NOT touched.
delete.needsForce: {{name}} has bound Releases. Use force-delete to detach them first.

mediaManagement.editorHint: Library create + edit forms (paths, lifecycle policy, profile bindings, exporter wiring) land in a follow-up slice.

platforms.title: Platform Packs
platforms.subtitle: Bulk platform definitions are shipped as YAML packs (built-in or community). This page audits every pack that has been applied. Upload + re-apply land in a follow-up slice.

empty.title: No packs applied yet
empty.body: The built-in pack should ship with Romarr. If this list is empty, restart the server to seed it.

platforms.author: by {{author}}

history.title: Application history
history.empty: No history rows logged for this pack.

platforms.uploadHint: Pack upload (multipart YAML) + per-platform override toggles land in a follow-up slice.

general.title: General
general.subtitle: Operator account settings. Today's slice covers personal API keys; richer surfaces (password change, OIDC unlink, login history) land as their endpoints surface.

empty.title: No API keys minted
empty.body: Mint a key from the form above to script Romarr from notifiarr / scripts / dashboards.

create.title: Mint a new key
create.subtitle: Pick a name and tick the permissions you want to grant. The plaintext is shown exactly once.
create.scopesNote: Three-tier ladder: admin implies write implies read. Tick the highest tier you need (lower tiers are implied server-side).

read.label: Read
read.hint: List games, releases, queue, history. Read-only access to every GET endpoint.

write.label: Write
write.hint: Create / edit games, releases, profiles, indexers, download clients. Implies Read.

admin.label: Admin
admin.hint: User management, Prowlarr applications, library deletion, system config. Implies Write.

created.title: Key minted — copy it now
created.body: {{name}} — the plaintext is shown ONCE and will not be retrievable later. Store it in your secrets manager.
created.warn: This key will not be shown again. Copy it now.

revoke.confirmBody: {{name}} will stop authenticating immediately. Any caller using this key will need a new one.

users.subtitle: Every account that can sign in. Create + edit forms land in a follow-up slice; delete is wired today.

empty.title: No users
empty.body: Romarr always seeds at least one admin during setup. If you see this, something is wrong with the auth migration.

delete.confirmBody: {{username}} will lose access immediately. Their API keys and notifications are revoked.

create.title: Add a new user
create.success: {{username}} created. They can sign in now.

metadataSources.title: Metadata Sources
metadataSources.subtitle: Per-field aggregation across the nine documented providers (IGDB, ScreenScraper, MobyGames, LaunchBox, SteamGridDB, RetroAchievements, HowLongToBeat, Hasheous, PlayMatch). Enable, prioritize, and test each one here.

empty.title: No metadata providers
empty.body: The default provider catalogue should ship with Romarr. If this list is empty, run the seed migration.

liveBadge.label: Active and healthy
liveBadge.title: Enabled, credentials valid, last health check OK

priority.label: Priority
priority.help: Lower number wins ties when two providers carry the same field.

configure.title: Configure {{provider}}
configure.subtitle: Credentials are Fernet-encrypted before being persisted.
configure.noCreds: This provider needs no credentials — it's public or free.

metadataSources.fieldPriorityHint: Per-field provider order is configured at /api/v3/metadata/field-priority — the drag-and-drop editor lands in a follow-up slice.

indexers.title: Indexers
indexers.subtitle: Newznab + Torznab sources Romarr searches when grabbing a release. Prowlarr-managed indexers sync automatically.

search.label: Search indexers
search.noMatches: No indexers match the active search.

applications.subtitle: Registered Prowlarr instances that push indexers into Romarr. Sync level controls whether Prowlarr can also pull state back.
applications.empty: No Prowlarr instances registered. The recommended setup is to add Romarr as a Prowlarr application — Prowlarr will then push indexers here automatically.
applications.unregisterConfirm: Unregister Prowlarr application "{{name}}"? Indexers it pushed will remain but won't receive future updates.
applications.rotateConfirm: Rotate the token for "{{name}}"? The old token stops working immediately; paste the new one into Prowlarr → Settings → Apps.

rotated.title: New token minted — copy it now
rotated.body: The old token is revoked. Paste this into Prowlarr → Settings → Apps → Romarr → Application Token.

register.title: Register a Prowlarr instance
register.subtitle: Romarr will pull the indexer list from Prowlarr. You'll get an app token to paste into Prowlarr for the reverse-sync channel.
register.successBody: Copy the Romarr API key below then paste it into Prowlarr — Settings → Apps → Sonarr → API Key.
register.tokenWarn: This Romarr API key is shown EXACTLY ONCE. Copy it now. If you lose it, use "Rotate token" on the row to mint a fresh one.
register.tokenLabel: Romarr API key (paste into Prowlarr's "API Key" field)

after.step1: In Prowlarr → Settings → Apps → click "+" → choose **Sonarr** (Romarr is Sonarr v3 compatible).
after.step2: Sonarr URL: http://romarr:8585 (or the network URL of Romarr). Prowlarr URL: leave Prowlarr's own.
after.step3: API Key: paste the Romarr key above. Sync Categories: pick what you want pushed. Test → Save.

register.sonarrCompatNote: ℹ Why "Sonarr"? Prowlarr doesn't natively know about Romarr yet, but Romarr exposes a Sonarr v3 compatible API (constitution Article VII), so picking "Sonarr" as the application type works.

howTo.title: Where do I find the Prowlarr API key?
howTo.step2: Section Security → API Key (32-character hex string).
howTo.step3: Copy it and paste it below. This is the key Prowlarr generated when it was installed, not a Romarr key.

field.name: Name (free-form, for your records)
field.apiKeyHint: Visible at Prowlarr → Settings → General → API Key. A single all-permissions key per instance — no scope selection on Prowlarr's side.

full_sync.label: Full sync
full_sync.hint: Romarr reads + Prowlarr can also push updates here (recommended).

add_only.label: Add only
add_only.hint: Prowlarr can add new indexers but won't modify existing ones.

disabled.label: Disabled
disabled.hint: Registration kept but no automatic sync.

empty.title: No indexers configured
empty.body: Add an indexer manually below, or push one from Prowlarr — Romarr is registered as a Prowlarr application and accepts pushed sources.

create.subhead: Manual entry for indexers that aren't pushed by Prowlarr. Most operators should register Romarr as a Prowlarr application instead.
create.implementationHint: Newznab is the canonical Usenet API; Torznab is the torrent variant. Both formats are interchangeable for the search engine.
create.urlHint: For Prowlarr: a specific indexer's URL (e.g. http://prowlarr:9696/5). Romarr appends /api?t=caps automatically. For a direct Newznab/Torznab: the service's root URL.
create.apiKeyHint: For Prowlarr: the same Prowlarr API key (Prowlarr → Settings → General → API Key, 32-char hex). For a direct Newznab/Torznab: the key your indexer gave you.
create.prowlarrHint: Tip: prefer the Prowlarr push setup. Add Romarr to your Prowlarr instance and the indexers sync over without you maintaining the manual entry below.

edit.subhead: Update the name, URL, or search modes. Leave the API key blank to keep the existing one.
edit.apiKeyPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the existing key
edit.apiKeyHint: Enter a new key only if you want to rotate the stored one.

test.emptyCapsHint: The indexer returned an empty response. If this is Prowlarr, the URL must be a specific indexer's path (e.g. http://prowlarr:9696/5) — not the root URL. Find it in Prowlarr → Indexers → click the indexer → the Newznab/Torznab URL is shown there.

delete.confirmBody: Searches won't include {{name}} anymore. This is reversible — re-add the same source via Prowlarr or the manual form.

unidentified.title: Unidentified
unidentified.subtitle: Files the importer couldn't auto-identify. Match each one to a Game + Release, or delete the row (the file on disk is preserved).

empty.title: No unidentified dumps
empty.body: When the importer fails to identify a file with confidence, it lands here for operator triage.

actions.deleteConfirmBody: The source file on disk is NOT touched. Only the queue row is removed.

match.typeToSearch: Type at least one character to search.
match.noReleases: This game has no Releases yet. Create one first via the Game Detail page (coming soon).

tags.title: Tags
tags.subtitle: Polymorphic tags applied across Games, Indexers, Notifications, and Releases. Renaming a tag updates every entity it touches.

empty.title: No tags yet
empty.body: Create one above to start tagging Games, Indexers, Notifications, or Releases.

filter.noMatches: No tags match the active filter.

errors.conflict: A tag with that slug already exists.

row.inUseHint: Tag is assigned to one or more entities. Click "Force delete" to cascade-remove the assignments.
row.forcePrompt: Tag "{{label}}" is currently assigned to one or more entities. Force-delete the assignments?
row.usageTooltip_one: Tag is currently used by {{count}} entity
row.usageTooltip_other: Tag is currently used by {{count}} entities
row.viewGamesAria_one: View the {{count}} game tagged "{{label}}" in the Library
row.viewGamesAria_other: View the {{count}} games tagged "{{label}}" in the Library

ui.title: UI preferences
ui.subtitle: Theme, language, and other operator-facing display preferences.

theme.label: Theme
theme.help: Auto follows your operating system's prefers-color-scheme setting.

language.label: Language
language.help: Applies immediately. Stored locally under romarr.lang.

install.label: Install Romarr
install.help: Add Romarr to your home screen for a full-screen experience and offline reads.
